Dispatched by the factory from `dev.task` [`b6164269-d8e8-42e1-9f3e-3c55c9d4b111`](b6164269-d8e8-42e1-9f3e-3c55c9d4b111).

**This PR was written by an agent and checked by the dispatcher.** The dispatcher
runs declared verification in the isolated clone before opening a PR. It
bootstraps a clone-local `venv/` from the repo's Python dependency declarations
and adds `PyYAML` because the committed EA/checker scripts import `yaml` without
owning that dependency in a requirements file. That path is slower than relying
on the host interpreter, but it keeps task specs faithful and makes
`venv/bin/python ...`, `python ...`, and `python3 ...` declarations resolve
inside the clone.

Change kind: behavioral

## Verification checkout

Declared verification below ran against `42e52426064aa26d6a245b96e7a9f3bcdaebafdc` of `main`. The dispatcher refuses to clone (so this PR would not exist) unless both hold at dispatch time: the worker checkout's own revision is a confirmed, current ancestor of local `main` (`worker_revision.ensure_checkout_is_current_with_main`), and `main` itself is a confirmed ancestor-or-equal of its own tracking upstream -- carries no commit absent from it (`dispatch.ensure_base_ref_current`; `BaseRefStatus.wrong`). Date this evidence against that commit, not against when the PR was opened.

This attempt resumed from preserved work: the latest of https://github.com/grantbest/homelabv2/pull/1185 was applied as the clone's starting point before the worker's first action (OPS-106). The revision above is the base the baseline was applied onto, not the tree verification ran against -- that tree is base + baseline + this attempt's work.

## Intent

Common rules from the design §8: dispatch.py and guards.py are unchanged (the pair is 8,530 lines at main 447d6174 and every merge must stay strictly below 8,556 [RE-BASELINED 2026-10-02 by the outer loop: the pair stood at 8,612 (7,229 + 1,383) at main 856071fe, so the absolute 8,556 no longer binds; the binding size rule is each bead's own net-growth bound in its ACs, measured against its own merge-base, and the arc closes at or below 8,612]); tests use fixtures and tmp_path only and never touch the live host or a real sudo (decision record 2026-09-13 D7); split mode means FACTORY_WORKER_USER is set and with it unset behaviour is today's byte for byte. Cross-uid facts (EACCES, EINVAL, the launchd session, Mach services, claude authenticating as uid 850) are proven only by the attended probe and the canaries (design §10), never by a test. Tests that execute sandbox-exec or chflags are darwin-only and are skipped off darwin with a stated reason, the idiom the existing sandbox tests use; CI is Linux and the factory's own pre-check runs them. Every spawn call passes env= (tests/test_spawn_inventory.py, MAX_UNFIXED_SPAWN_CALLS = 0). Design §8 row B3 (predecessor B2, here B2b; also B1 for the hash comparison function, both set at filing) and §10 steps 10-13 of the attended runbook. Mechanism: §3.1 the sudoers rule `Defaults>_factoryworker pam_service=factory-worker, !pam_setcred, !log_input, !log_output` and `grantbest ALL=(_factoryworker) NOPASSWD: /Users/Shared/factory/bin/factory-worker-launch` for /etc/sudoers.d/factory-worker (root:wheel 0440, installed with visudo by the Operator); §3.2 the PAM service /etc/pam.d/factory-worker (auth required pam_deny.so; account required pam_permit.so; password required pam_deny.so; session required pam_launchd.so), the only mechanism found that moves a sudo-started process out of grantbest's gui/501 session, whose effect is measured by probe item (a) and is explicitly unverified until then; §3.4 hash drift: worker_identity records at import the sha256 of worker_launcher.py and process_env.py beside its own file (B1 AC-8 exposes both, and a comparison function taking the installed copies' bytes), the claim compares the installed copies on the dispatcher side (850 cannot read the checkout), re-copies on mismatch (bin is grantbest-owned, the rule names a path not a hash, so no admin is needed), and if the re-copy fails pauses the dispatch schedule in the capacity-pause shape (_pause_schedule_for_capacity_failure, activities/dispatch_steps.py:1559 at 447d6174) and claims nothing; a claude version mismatch re-copies the binary. The runbook's step 10 command is `launchd_agent.py install-worker-identity --user _factoryworker --bin /Users/Shared/factory/bin`: it copies the launcher, process_env.py and the current claude binary, writes R/.worker-user (the user name, 0600, for purge after a rollback, §2.2), and prints the sudoers and PAM texts; step 12 is `probe-worker-identity --selfcheck`; step 13 is `probe-worker-identity`, attended. launchd_agent.py's existing shape: subcommands install/uninstall (:816-817), install-tunnel/uninstall-tunnel/verify-tunnel (:883-889), render_plist (:332), render_tunnel_plist (:437), render_keeper_watchdog_plist (:596), main (:958); it is a C-4 boundary path (file_task.BOUNDARY_PATHS), hence the principal and reaches above.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-1: GOLDEN SUDOERS AND PAM TEXT, PRINTED ONLY. Two pure functions render the sudoers file text and the PAM file text from (user, launcher path) exactly as the design's §3.1 and §3.2 give them, byte for byte including the comment headers naming the paths and modes; `install-worker-identity` prints both under headings that say where the Operator installs each and with which command (visudo -f; install -m 0644 -o root -g wheel). Nothing under /etc is read or written by any code path in this bead (a test monkeypatches open/os functions to raise on any /etc path and runs the subcommand end to end in tmp_path). When `visudo` is on PATH, a test runs `visudo -c -f <tmp file>` on the rendered sudoers text and asserts exit 0; otherwise that test is skipped with a reason.
- AC-2: INSTALL COPIES AND RECORDS. With --bin <dir> and --runs-root <R> (defaults /Users/Shared/factory/bin and /Users/Shared/factory-runs, module constants shared with worker_identity's), `install-worker-identity` copies worker_launcher.py as `factory-worker-launch` (mode 0755) and process_env.py (0644) from the running checkout into <bin>, copies the claude binary as <bin>/claude, resolved by shutil.which of the claude WorkerEntry's argv[0] (the same name dispatch.py resolves inline at :2595; there is no shared resolver function to import, so launchd_agent does the same which() through an injectable resolver parameter) followed by os.path.realpath, because on this host `claude` is a symlink to the Mach-O under ~/.local/share and the copy must be the real binary, writes <R>/.worker-user containing the user name at 0600, and prints what it wrote with the sha256 of each copy. It refuses, writing nothing, when <bin> or <R> is not a directory owned by the effective uid, or when a destination exists as a symlink. Tests run it entirely in tmp_path with an injected claude resolver and assert contents, modes and hashes.
- AC-3: THE HASH CHECK AND RE-COPY. A function `check_installed_worker_identity(bin_dir, hashes)` reads the installed launcher and process_env.py bytes and calls B1's comparison function; on mismatch or missing it re-copies the mismatched file and re-checks; it returns a small frozen result (per file: match | recopied | failed, with the reason). It is pure apart from the injected file operations (an `ops` parameter with read/copy/stat, defaulting to the real ones), so tests cover match, mismatch-then-recopied, missing-then-recopied, and recopy-failing (the fake raises) without touching a real bin. The claim-side call (deciding to pause) is B4b's; this bead exposes the function and documents the capacity-pause shape it is meant to feed.
- AC-4: PROBE AND SELFCHECK THROUGH THE LAUNCHER. `probe-worker-identity --selfcheck` and `probe-worker-identity` build the sudo launch call with B1's launch-call builder for the `selfcheck` and `probe` subcommands, run it through an injected runner, and print the launcher's envelope as indented JSON with each probe item labelled by the runbook's letter and its design meaning; they decide nothing and print the design's closure precondition for 75b50b58 as text beneath the observations, for the operator. Tests use a recording fake runner and assert the exact argv and env (PATH only) for both, and that the runner is never called twice.
- AC-5: WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE. The existing subcommands, their renderers and their tests are unchanged; dispatch.py, guards.py and activities/** are untouched; nothing in this bead is wired into claim or install. The PR body states that the admin steps (visudo, the PAM file, the account) are the Operator's and are not performed by any code here. Every new spawn-bearing function this bead adds (the population tests/spawn_scan.py's find_spawn_calls discovers, keyed (path, function)) gets its own entry in CASES in tests/test_spawn_env_fixture.py exercising that function with the recorder, so test_every_spawn_bearing_function_has_a_case stays green; spawns go through a plain `import subprocess` and `subprocess.run`/`subprocess.Popen` resolved at call time, because that fixture patches them as attributes of the shared module.
- AC-6: MUTATION. Each turns a test red: writing the sudoers text to /etc; granting a runas other than the worker user in the rendered rule; omitting !log_input or !log_output; writing .worker-user with group or other bits; copying over a symlinked destination; reporting match for a mismatched hash; calling the runner with an env beyond PATH.
- AC-7: STAGE AND REPORT. git add new files before the final run; the PR body states the collected-test count before and after, the two rendered texts verbatim, and whether visudo -c ran.

## Declared scope

Allowed: apps/factory-dispatcher/launchd_agent.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/tests/
Forbidden: .github/**, .github/workflows/**, .gitignore, AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, apps/factory-dispatcher/activities/**, apps/factory-dispatcher/containment.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/dispatch.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/file_task.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/guards.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/process_env.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/tasks/**, apps/factory-dispatcher/tests/fixtures/**, apps/factory-dispatcher/worker.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/worker_identity.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/worker_launcher.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/workflows/**, apps/lifeops-console/**, apps/mcp-hub/**, apps/substrate/**, docs/**, infrastructure/**, scripts/**

Dispatcher scope verdict: **all changes within scope**

## Verification the task asked for

- `cd apps/factory-dispatcher && python -m pytest tests/test_launchd_agent.py tests/test_boundary_principal.py tests/test_spawn_env_fixture.py -q`
- `cd apps/factory-dispatcher && python -m pytest tests/ -q`
- `python scripts/check-repo-invariants.py`

## Environment parity with CI

- **Neutralized:** ambient git config. Declared verification runs with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` pointed at `/dev/null` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` set, so `init.defaultBranch` and any committer identity from the operator's `~/.gitconfig`, a conventional `/etc/gitconfig`, *or* a vendor-baked installation-scope config (Apple's git ships one CI has no equivalent of -- PR #792's gate caught that `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` alone doesn't hide it) are invisible to it, matching a CI runner that has none of the three (#765's `create_repo_with_tracking_main` specimen).
- **Reported, not neutralized:** this clone carries a local `main` branch tracking `origin/main`, because the dispatcher's own later git operations in this same clone need one. CI's `actions/checkout` on a PR instead leaves a detached HEAD with no local `main`. A declared command that depends on `main` being a resolvable ref -- not merely on config -- can still pass here and fail in CI (#759).
- **Undetectable by this pre-check:** anything not git-configuration or dependency-presence shaped -- network reachability, OS/platform differences, resource limits, and any ambient environment variable outside `VERIFICATION_ENV_ALLOWLIST` that CI also lacks. A green pre-check establishes parity only for the two points above, not general CI-equivalence.

## Worker's own report

```
Interpreter used for all verification: a clone-local venv built at `$TMPDIR/venv-factory-dispatcher` from `apps/factory-dispatcher/requirements.txt` (never `/Users/grantbest/Documents/Active.nosync/venv`).

Items 1-8, each with its proving test and mutation result:

1. **argv/env exactness (recorder tests).** `test_run_selfcheck_probe_calls_the_runner_exactly_once_and_prints_the_envelope` and `test_run_worker_probe_calls_the_runner_exactly_once_and_labels_items` now assert the full `argv` tuple, `env == {"PATH": wi.MINIMAL_PATH}`, and the exact payload key set (`{}` for selfcheck, `{"paths","mach_names","target_pid"}` for probe). Manually verified red: widening `worker_identity.build_launch_call`'s env (e.g. adding a second key) and adding a key to `default_probe_fields()` both fail the new assertions; reverted after confirming.

2. **install-worker-identity never driven through `main()`.** Added `test_main_install_worker_identity_writes_every_file_through_the_cli`, which runs the real CLI via `launchd_agent.main([...])` against `tmp_path`, with PATH pointed at a fake `claude` and `FACTORY_OPERATOR_ACCOUNT` set, and asserts every written file's bytes and mode. Widened the `/etc` guard test to also patch `launchd_agent.os.open`. Manually verified red: swapping `args.bin_dir`/`args.runs_root` in `main()`, deleting the install call, and routing a write through `os.open("/etc/...")` each fail the respective test.

3. **Hash-recopy mismatch-after-recopy.** Added `test_check_installed_worker_identity_refuses_when_recopy_still_mismatches`: a fake `copy` that succeeds but writes the wrong bytes. The existing post-copy re-check in `check_installed_worker_identity` already reports `"failed"`/`"hash still does not match after recopy"` — confirmed by temporarily deleting that re-check (reporting `"recopied"` unconditionally), which turns the new test red; reverted.

4. **Atomicity.** Added `_atomic_write_bytes` (O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY|O_NOFOLLOW temp file, `os.fchmod`, `fsync`, `os.replace`), used for the launcher, process_env.py, claude binary, `.worker-user`, and the hash-check recopy. `test_install_worker_identity_replaces_destinations_atomically_changing_inode` proves the inode changes across a re-install; `test_install_worker_identity_recopy_leaves_other_hardlinks_untouched` proves a separately-held hardlink's bytes survive a re-install untouched.

5. **Hostile targets.** `_require_not_symlink` generalized to `_require_safe_destination` (refuses symlink/directory/FIFO/other, allows a pre-existing regular file). New tests: `test_install_worker_identity_refuses_when_a_destination_is_a_directory`, `test_install_worker_identity_refuses_when_a_destination_is_a_fifo`, each asserting no file at all gets written.

6. **Modes.** `_require_bin_dir_not_writable_by_others` (refuses group/world-writable bin) and `_require_runs_root_has_no_group_or_other_bits` (refuses any group/other bit). New tests cover bin at 0777 and runs-root at 0755, each refused before any write. This required fixing every existing `install_worker_identity` test's directory setup (bare `.mkdir()` inherits the ambient umask, 0755) to create `runs_root` at 0700 via a new `_mkdir_mode` helper — a mechanical test-setup fix, not a behavior change.

7. **Names.** `ACCOUNT_NAME_PATTERN = ^[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$`, applied to both `--user` and the resolved `--operator`, plus explicit `"root"` refusal and a `user == operator` refusal. New tests: parametrized invalid-user names (`root`, `ALL`, `User`, embedded space, leading dash, 33 chars), an operator string containing a newline + `ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL` (asserts nothing is printed), and user-equals-operator.

8. **Probe honesty.** `PROBE_ITEM_LABELS["e"]` now says `NOT RUN` (no claude payload is sent); `"g"`/`"h"` now say `NOT MEASURED IN THE WORKER PROFILE` instead of claiming "inside the worker profile". `test_probe_item_labels_say_what_was_actually_measured_not_what_was_intended` pins this down.

Collected-test count: **301
```

## Report completion (outer loop, 2026-10-04)

The worker's report above ends at "Collected-test count: **301" because the dispatcher's PR template cuts the report off at 4,000 characters without saying so. That truncation is a template defect, being fixed under OPS-3dc4a938. The figures below were measured by the release gate on head aab34f33, not reconstructed from the lost text.

- Collected tests (`cd apps/factory-dispatcher && python -m pytest tests/ --collect-only -q`): **3013 at merge base 42e52426, 3059 at head aab34f33 (+46)**. Declared command 1: 134 passed. Full suite: 3059 passed, 0 skipped. `scripts/check-repo-invariants.py`: passed.
- `visudo -c -f <tmp file>` ran in the test suite as a non-root syntax check and exited 0. It is the only process any test spawns. No test runs sudo, dscl, launchctl, chown or a real install.
- **The admin steps are the Operator's, and no code in this PR performs them:** creating the `_factoryworker` account, installing the sudoers rule with `sudo visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/factory-worker`, and installing the PAM file at `/etc/pam.d/factory-worker`. `install-worker-identity` only prints these two texts. It writes only the grantbest-owned `bin` and `runs-root` contents.

Rendered sudoers text, from `render_worker_sudoers_text("_factoryworker", "/Users/Shared/factory/bin/factory-worker-launch", "<operator>")` (the operator name is a parameter, so no household identifier is compiled in):

    # /etc/sudoers.d/factory-worker   root:wheel 0440, installed with visudo
    Defaults>_factoryworker pam_service=factory-worker, !pam_setcred, !log_input, !log_output
    <operator> ALL=(_factoryworker) NOPASSWD: /Users/Shared/factory/bin/factory-worker-launch

Rendered PAM text, from `render_worker_pam_text()`:

    # /etc/pam.d/factory-worker   root:wheel 0644
    auth       required   pam_deny.so
    account    required   pam_permit.so
    password   required   pam_deny.so
    session    required   pam_launchd.so
